subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class skill-creation authority/pre-selection hook, rely on existing plugin tools plus prompt guidance, or keep this as a ClawHub/workflow convention outside core?
rationale: The requested behavior changes plugin API semantics, tool routing, optional config, and governed skill-write policy, so source inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design a narrow authority hook
options.body: Add a maintainer-owned plugin/API design for skill-creation authority that runs before `skill_workshop` selection and still submits final content through Skill Workshop.

options.title: Use existing tools and prompts
options.body: Document the supported pattern as custom tools preparing proposal content and then calling `skill_workshop`, without adding new routing authority.

options.title: Move to ClawHub convention
options.body: Keep core unchanged and ask custom skill-creation workflows to ship as ClawHub skills or plugins that users invoke explicitly.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authority hook
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-owned plugin/API design for skill-creation authority that runs before `skill_workshop` selection and still submits final content through Skill Workshop.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the core Skill Workshop proposal/tool architecture and is the strongest history-based owner for the API boundary choice.
